about: Step 0.6. For every field of Horde's session record: its one future owner, and until that field is switched over, the order in which the old stores are read when they disagree. The old systems' duplication is recorded here as reading rules, not repaired. A store's guard applies to every read of that store, before the read's own when. Every field of the record is named in required and is either kept in fields or listed in dropped with its reason. Evidence for every rule: planning/ledger/core-ownership.md.

owners.agent: the agent's own control file, read through the AgentPort
owners.host: the terminal host adapter, read live; never identity

W2.guard: the claim for the session's pane, read only while that session has no registry record (the hook consumes a claim on first sight and deletes it), whose spawnedAt is at most 10080 minutes old, and whose cwd matches the session's cwd when both are recorded

X1.guard: the file passes every check Read-WfPaneSessionFile makes - a numeric pane, only one wezterm-gui running, a well-formed session_id, and written after this terminal instance started - its pane is live and it is the only live pane-sessions file naming that session, and no live X2 session contradicts it (the hijack case)

X6.path: WEZTERM_PANE, WEZFLEET_SESSION_ID, CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID and others; inherited, so can be wrong

storeIdGaps.W7: No store is numbered W7. The ids were fixed when the table was drafted and are kept rather than renumbered, so citations of W8 stay valid. Which store the draft numbered W7 is in no committed file. The wezfleet stores this table does not list are read by no field of the session record: mail, registry\labels (label reservation markers; the allocator derives its counter from the registry itself), the run index, the delivery and raw-send logs, and locks.

read.when: only for a session asking who it is itself; the variable is inherited, so it never identifies another pane

fields.name: agent
fields.derived: which agent's control-file directory the session id was found in

read.when: its --resume id matches

not retired, and written in this terminal instance: the record's instance matches this one when the record names one, and its lastSeen, the time the hook last saw a tool call, is not before the instance started. No age limit, as census reads it
a record older than firstCwd

fields.name: transcriptPath
fields.derived: Claude: from sessionId and projectCwd, then checked to exist. Codex: from its control file until a derivation is measured

read.when: the transcript it names exists

fields.name: resumeCommand
fields.derived: computed by the AgentPort from the agent kind and session id
fields.provisional: the installed wezterm-resurrect and its main branch take the session id in opposite orders; which one the shadow compares against is undecided

read.when: shadow comparison only; never trusted as the answer
shadow comparison only; a stored copy, written at report time as claude --resume and the id

fields.name: pane
fields.derived: the live host handle, recorded in a realisation; never identity
fields.provisional: reading the pane-sessions file (X1) before the status snapshot (W5) is a Horde decision: no single wezfleet function reads both - census reads the registry then X1, the run snapshot reads roster, then status, then registry - so which is right when they disagree is for the shadow to measure

read.when: not retired, and written in this terminal instance: the record's instance matches this one when the record names one, and its lastSeen, the time the hook last saw a tool call, is not before the instance started. No age limit - census and the finder that picks a pane to act on read it this way; the 900-second limit of the run snapshot and Get-WfPaneIdentity is not adopted, so a session quiet for longer keeps its registry pane here and there falls back to status or roster
run-level; fallback only: the window the run owns, which a session that moved windows is no longer in

fields.name: hostInstance
fields.derived: from the terminal's socket, which names the instance exactly; with no socket, from the one terminal process running; with no socket and more than one terminal process running, the instance is ambiguous, and an ambiguous instance trusts no pane record

read.when: for the session's own process, which inherits it from its pane
as the hook took it from the socket at the session's last tool call
exactly one terminal process is running

fields.name: owner
fields.derived: the parent's label, else founder; display only, never an edge

read.when: display only
display only
within its TTL, except ended, which never expires

fields.name: workState
fields.derived: from reported events, liveness and activity; terminal events are trusted outright

read.when: false means pending
the log is the truth; status.json is only its cache

fields.name: lastActivity
fields.derived: the newest of the command logs, the transcript's write time, and the agent's own status time

read.when: only for a session asking which run it is in itself, and only when that directory exists

the roster lists the session's fleet id. Among open runs (run.json has no closedAt) the one that spawned it wins; two open runs that both spawned it, or several open runs none of which did, are ambiguous and reported, never chosen; a closed run is used only when no open run lists it
present; entries written before the field have none, and absent reads as unknown, never as fresh

fields.name: procStart
fields.derived: the process's creation time in Windows file-time ticks; a pid is the same process only while its creation time is unchanged, since a reused pid has a different start

fields.name: formerNames
fields.provisional: each former name carries a sessionId; whether that is an earlier id of this same conversation or another conversation shown in this process is unmeasured

dropped.name: remoteControl
dropped.reason: wezfleet's registry has the field and Set-WfSessionFields accepts it, but no shipped caller passes it, so it is always empty; whether a session is bridged for remote control is the agent's own bridgeSessionId, read from its control file
